task: rerun only Changed Steps on stage and prod deploys (MAP #18 part 2, per next-horizon-brief.md)

analysis.objective: Make every stage and prod deploy run `adops run --all --changed --env <env>` so that each Pipeline is rerun in full, rerun from its first Changed Step, or marked 'unchanged, nothing rerun' by the binding horizon-17 Deploy Rerun Rules. This finishes MAP #18 on top of horizon 17's release folders.
analysis.successDefinition: (1) A framework-free domain rule returns one Deploy Plan per Pipeline: full, from-step <name>, or unchanged. It picks full when the Environment's Settings Marker changed (that affects every Pipeline), when the Pipeline has a new Accepted-Change Record, when the Pipeline has no Schedule, or when it has no saved Step Fingerprints. Otherwise it reruns from first_changed_step. If no Step changed, the Pipeline is unchanged. Unit tests cover each branch of the rule and the order the rules are checked in. (2) Prod saves its own Step Fingerprints in prod's Warehouse adops schema after Checks pass, just as stage does. Saved rows for Steps that are no longer in a Pipeline are pruned, or ignored by a by-name comparison. Tests show that Branch deferral against stage behaves exactly as before. (3) Each Environment keeps its own Deploy State in its own Warehouse: the Settings Marker, which is a canonical hash of the parsed settings for that Environment's own block plus the shared parts (Sources, timezone, top-level settings), and the Accepted-Change Record ids it has seen. Tests show that a comment edit, a formatting edit or an edit to another Environment's block does not change the marker, while a change to a Source in that Environment's own block does (adops.yaml has no cross-Environment Sources). Deploy State is written only after the deploy passes, so a failed deploy reruns the same work next time. (4) `adops run --all --changed` runs only with --all and --env stage|prod. It exits with a clear, sanitized error when used without --all, with --branch, with dev, or with a single PIPELINE. `adops run --all` without --changed still runs every Pipeline. Skipped Steps get their own status and Run Log/output wording ('unchanged in <env>'), never the Branch wording 'deferred to stage'. A Pipeline with nothing to rerun writes an 'unchanged, nothing rerun' line. (5) The generated adops-stage.yml and adops-prod.yml run `adops run --all --changed --env <env> --project /project/current`. The tests in tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py assert this by parsing the YAML (g7). (6) The repo gates pass: 100% line and branch coverage with no pragma (g2/g5), no framework imports in domain/application (g6), templates ship in the wheel (g3), and the full e2e job stays under 20 minutes (g4) with at most one added cheap stage e2e check. That check shows a second deploy with only one dbt model changed reruns from that Transform Step and leaves the unchanged Sync alone. (7) ADR-0006, ADR-0014 and ADR-0016 and promotion.md each get a dated clarification. They state that deploys rerun only Changed Steps, that prod saves fingerprints, and that scheduled Pipelines whose Steps did not change no longer refresh on merge. They also record a real-runner retrial as a follow-up. The decisions.md lines for this horizon are recorded.
assumptions: confirmed: 'any adops.yaml change' means a change to a canonical hash of the parsed settings that affect the deployed Environment only: that Environment's own block plus shared parts (Sources, timezone, top-level settings). Comments, formatting and other Environments' blocks do not count.

confirmed: the CLI surface is a new flag `adops run --all --changed`, valid only together with --all and --env stage|prod. Hand use of `adops run --all` keeps running every Pipeline. Both generated deploy workflows (adops-stage.yml, adops-prod.yml) switch to it.

confirmed: this horizon has no real-runner or manual trial. Proof is unit tests plus at most one cheap stage e2e check, because the full e2e job already takes 17:11 of its 20-minute budget. A real-runner retrial is a recorded follow-up.

Horizon 17 shipped as described. It is commit d485946: release_folders.py, release_command.py (`adops server-release`), the per-run adops/release tag, and deploys that run against /project/current. The held-run e2e case is green.

The horizon-17 decisions are binding and are not reopened. They supersede horizon 8's 'merge->stage runs every Pipeline'. They fix the Deploy Rerun Rules (new record -> that Pipeline in full; Settings Marker change -> every Pipeline; no Schedule -> full; no saved fingerprints -> full; otherwise from the first Changed Step). They also say prod saves its own Step Fingerprints.

Deploy State lives in each Environment's own Warehouse adops schema, next to the Step Fingerprints and _adops_applied_records. It does not live in .adops or on the Server filesystem, so it survives release-folder switches and needs no new Server volume.

An Accepted-Change Record counts as 'new' for a deploy when its id is not yet in that Environment's saved seen-record set. Existing applied-record storage is reused or widened when it can state this. A separate seen-ids table is added only if applied-only-when-a-Sync-runs cannot express it.

Deploy State and new fingerprints are written only after each Pipeline's run passes. A failed Step therefore leaves no new fingerprint for itself or for later Steps, and the next deploy reruns from that Step.
The first deploy after upgrade has no saved prod fingerprints or Deploy State, so it runs every Pipeline in full. That is the intended safe default.
The changed-only planning reuses run_pipeline's existing `first` slicing. Only the skipped-Step status and wording change from the Branch path.

The dangling .adops link bug in prepare_release (FileExistsError from Path.mkdir(parents=True)) is fixed in this horizon. It is a small, already-diagnosed infrastructure fix that the horizon-17 notes put in horizon 18.
confirmed: 6 phases accepted (the .adops link fix stays its own phase).
confirmed: the first deploy after upgrade runs every Pipeline in full.
confirmed: overlapping scheduled and deploy runs are serialized by the Warehouse lock; no extra ordering.
confirmed: scheduled prod Server runs saving Step Fingerprints is intended.
risks: Prod's Warehouse role may lack CREATE on the adops schema. Saving prod Step Fingerprints and Deploy State for the first time could then fail the first upgraded prod deploy. Nobody has checked this. A clear error and a playbook note are needed.

A scheduled full run on the old release can overlap a deploy's changed-only run of the same Pipeline. If the scheduled run saves its own fingerprints after the deploy saved new ones, the saved state no longer matches the data. The per-Pipeline Warehouse lock and run pinning must order the writes, or a scheduled run must not overwrite fingerprints from a newer release.
Pruning stale fingerprint rows in stage could change how Branch deferral resolves Steps today and break existing Branch e2e behaviour.

Defining the canonical settings hash wrongly creates two failure modes. If it is too narrow, a real connection change (for example a shared Source) is missed and stale code runs. If it is too wide, every deploy reruns everything and the feature delivers nothing.

Documented behaviour change: an unchanged scheduled Pipeline no longer refreshes on merge, and a skipped Incremental Sync stays stale until its next Schedule. Users who relied on merge-triggered refreshes may read this as a regression. Pipelines with no Schedule still run in full, which matches ADR-0014's 'runs only then'.

The e2e budget has only about 2:49 of headroom. Any changed-only e2e case on both Warehouses could push the job past 20 minutes (g4). The added check should run on one Warehouse only, or extend an existing deploy case.
Reusing the 'deferred' StepStatus or the Branch wording for deploy skips would mislead users and the Assistant about why a Step did not run.
Writing Deploy State before the run, or recording seen record ids when a Sync Step was skipped, could stop a new Accepted-Change Record from ever being applied in that Environment.
Renaming saves_stage_fingerprint or the fingerprint store or port to an Environment-neutral name touches many call sites and tests. It could cost more than the horizon's phase ceiling allows.
outOfScope: Changing hand-typed `adops run --all` or single-Pipeline `adops run`: the user confirmed they keep running every Step.
Branch Environment behaviour (PR runs deferring to stage): it is already changed-only by ADR-0006 and must not change.
Scheduled Server runs: they keep running their Pipeline in full on the Schedule. Only deploy-triggered runs change.
dev Environment changed-only runs: the flag is valid only for stage and prod, and dev has no saved fingerprints by design.
A real self-hosted-runner or Mac retrial of the changed-only deploy: the user excluded it, and it is recorded as a follow-up.
Deploy rollback or switching 'current' back to an earlier release: it is a separate concern and not part of the rerun rules.
Freshness alerts (MAP #19), including alerting on Pipelines left stale by skipped deploy reruns: a later horizon.
Git-diff-based change detection: decision h6 fixed fingerprint comparison with no Git, and the Server image has no git.
Moving existing Servers to new storage or layout: Deploy State goes into the existing Warehouse adops schema, and the release-folder migration was finished in horizon 17.
Rerunning only the Steps downstream of a changed Step, instead of every Step from the first Changed Step onward: the binding rule reruns from the first Changed Step in Pipeline order.
Retry behaviour (the 3x300 s RetryRequested path) for in-process deploy runs: it applies to Server runs only and is unchanged.

phases.name: Fix the dangling .adops link in prepare_release
phases.goal: A Server root that has no .adops folder yet can be switched to a new release folder, and Syncs then run from it without a FileExistsError.
phases.rationale: prepare_release (horizon 17) links releases/<commit>/.adops to the Server root's .adops even when that folder does not exist. dlt then calls mkdir(parents=True) through the broken link and fails with FileExistsError. The fix is small and already diagnosed, and nothing else in this horizon depends on it.
changes: In prepare_release, create server_dir/.adops with mkdir(exist_ok=True) before the .adops link is made, so the link always points at a real folder.
Add a unit test that prepares a release in a Server root without .adops, then creates a nested folder through the release's .adops link (as dlt's local state dir does) and asserts it succeeds.
Keep the existing .env link behaviour and its tests unchanged.
phases.expectedResult: prepare_release creates server_dir/.adops before linking, proven by a unit test in tests/unit/infrastructure/test_release_folders.py for a Server root without .adops.
guardNotes: g2: the new mkdir line is covered by the new unit test, so line and branch coverage stays at 100%.

rubric.label: The release's .adops link always points at a real folder
rubric.ruleStatement: After prepare_release runs on a Server root that has no .adops folder, server_dir/.adops exists as a real directory and releases/<commit>/.adops resolves to it, so a nested mkdir through the link succeeds. 10 = a test also proves that an existing .adops folder and the files in it are kept as they are; 8 = the missing-folder case is proven by a test that does what dlt does (mkdir(parents=True) of a nested path through the link); minScore 8.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/test_release_folders.py -q`: it passes and includes a test that starts from a Server root with no .adops folder.

That test calls prepare_release, then runs `(release / '.adops' / 'a' / 'b').mkdir(parents=True)` (or a similar nested mkdir through the link) and asserts that it succeeds and that the new folder is under server_dir/.adops.
In src/adops/infrastructure/release_folders.py, server_dir/.adops is created with exist_ok=True before the links are made, not after os.replace.
Run `uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-report=term-missing`: release_folders.py shows 100% line and branch coverage and has no new pragma.
failureExamples: The test only asserts `(release / '.adops').is_symlink()`. That passes while the link still dangles, so the FileExistsError bug is not covered.
The folder is created inside the release folder (releases/<commit>/.adops as a real folder) instead of under server_dir. State then stops being shared across release switches.
mkdir runs without exist_ok, so preparing a second release for a Server root that already has .adops raises FileExistsError.

phases.name: Add Deploy Rerun Rules and Settings Marker
phases.goal: One pure function decides, for each Pipeline in a deploy, whether to rerun it in full, from its first Changed Step, or not at all ('unchanged'). A second pure function computes the Settings Marker for one Environment. Prod is allowed to save Step Fingerprints.
phases.rationale: The rules for which Pipelines a stage or prod deploy reruns are the core business decision of this horizon. They have to be testable without a Warehouse, so they live in the framework-free domain layer next to the existing first_changed_step. A Step Fingerprint is a hash of a Step's definition. A Changed Step is one whose fingerprint differs from the one the Environment saved after its last passing run. The Settings Marker is a hash of the adops.yaml settings that affect one Environment.

Add settings_marker(settings: ProjectSettings, env: str) -> str. It is the sha256 of canonical JSON (json.dumps(model_dump(mode='json'), sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')), the same pattern as canonical_step_json) of environments[env] (warehouse, sources, targets) plus timezone and alert_webhook_env. Comments, formatting and other Environments' blocks do not change it. It holds only secret-reference names, never secret values.

Add plan_deploy(pipeline, current_fingerprints, saved_fingerprints, marker_changed, unseen_record_ids) -> DeployPlan, where unseen_record_ids are this Pipeline's Accepted-Change Record ids (the caller filters records by r.pipeline == pipeline.name) minus DeployState.seen_record_ids. Check the rules in this binding order: Settings Marker changed -> full; any unseen Accepted-Change Record id for this Pipeline -> full; pipeline.schedule is None -> full; no saved fingerprints -> full; otherwise keep only saved rows whose Step name is in the current Pipeline and call first_changed_step; None -> unchanged, an index -> from_step.

phases.name: Add unchanged Step status to deploy runs
phases.goal: run_pipeline can run a stage or prod Pipeline from a given Step, or not at all. Steps it does not rerun get a new 'unchanged' status that counts as success. After the Pipeline passes, it saves the Pipeline's Accepted-Change Record ids as seen in the Environment's Deploy State.
phases.rationale: The existing 'deferred' status means 'a Branch run used stage's data' and 'skipped' means 'not run after a failure'. Reusing either for a deploy would mislead users and the Assistant about why a Step did not run. An Accepted-Change Record is a file that accepts a Breaking Change for one Pipeline. Deploy State is the per-Environment record of the last Settings Marker and the record ids already seen. Seen ids must be written only after a passing run, so a failed deploy redoes the same work next time.

successCriteria: Done when ALL hold: (1) A framework-free domain rule returns one Deploy Plan per Pipeline: full, from-step <name>, or unchanged. It picks full when the Environment's Settings Marker changed (that affects every Pipeline), when the Pipeline has a new Accepted-Change Record, when the Pipeline has no Schedule, or when it has no saved Step Fingerprints. Otherwise it reruns from first_changed_step. If no Step changed, the Pipeline is unchanged. Unit tests cover each branch of the rule and the order the rules are checked in. (2) Prod saves its own Step Fingerprints in prod's Warehouse adops schema after Checks pass, just as stage does. Saved rows for Steps that are no longer in a Pipeline are pruned, or ignored by a by-name comparison. Tests show that Branch deferral against stage behaves exactly as before. (3) Each Environment keeps its own Deploy State in its own Warehouse: the Settings Marker, which is a canonical hash of the parsed settings for that Environment's own block plus the shared parts (Sources, timezone, top-level settings), and the Accepted-Change Record ids it has seen. Tests show that a comment edit, a formatting edit or an edit to another Environment's block does not change the marker, while a change to a Source in that Environment's own block does (adops.yaml has no cross-Environment Sources). Deploy State is written only after the deploy passes, so a failed deploy reruns the same work next time. (4) `adops run --all --changed` runs only with --all and --env stage|prod. It exits with a clear, sanitized error when used without --all, with --branch, with dev, or with a single PIPELINE. `adops run --all` without --changed still runs every Pipeline. Skipped Steps get their own status and Run Log/output wording ('unchanged in <env>'), never the Branch wording 'deferred to stage'. A Pipeline with nothing to rerun writes an 'unchanged, nothing rerun' line. (5) The generated adops-stage.yml and adops-prod.yml run `adops run --all --changed --env <env> --project /project/current`. The tests in tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py assert this by parsing the YAML (g7). (6) The repo gates pass: 100% line and branch coverage with no pragma (g2/g5), no framework imports in domain/application (g6), templates ship in the wheel (g3), and the full e2e job stays under 20 minutes (g4) with at most one added cheap stage e2e check. That check shows a second deploy with only one dbt model changed reruns from that Transform Step and leaves the unchanged Sync alone. (7) ADR-0006, ADR-0014 and ADR-0016 and promotion.md each get a dated clarification. They state that deploys rerun only Changed Steps, that prod saves fingerprints, and that scheduled Pipelines whose Steps did not change no longer refresh on merge. They also record a real-runner retrial as a follow-up. The decisions.md lines for this horizon are recorded.
